moat_against: Only about 2% share of a fragmented US industrial distribution market — no dominant scale versus Grainger or Fastenal
Sells other manufacturers' branded products; suppliers can sell direct and customers can multi-source commodity parts
Demand is cyclical MRO/industrial production — FY2020-21 revenue was flat and OE is working-capital sensitive
Pricing power is service-based, not product-based: gross margin is only about 30% and operating margin about 11%
moat_for: Technical Engineered Solutions (fluid power, flow control, automation) — embedded engineering and specification work raises switching costs versus catalog distributors
ROIC proxy 19.3–21.0% in FY2023–FY2026 (fundamentals.json) with gross margin rising from 28.9% in FY2021 to 30.3% in FY2026
Dense local service-center network supplying critical MRO parts — customer downtime cost dwarfs the part cost, making availability and technical support sticky
Disciplined tuck-in M&A in a fragmented market plus buybacks — diluted share count is falling (share CAGR -1.17%)
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat: a technical, service-heavy distributor (Engineered Solutions in fluid power, flow control and automation, plus a dense Service Center MRO network) with ROIC proxy sustained at 19.3–21.0% in FY2023–FY2026 and gross margin edging up from 28.9% (FY2021) to 30.3% (FY2026) in fundamentals.json — evidence of real, service-based pricing power and returns well above the cost of capital through recent years. But it holds only about 2% of a fragmented market, sells other manufacturers' branded products that customers can multi-source, and its demand is cyclical industrial MRO, so the moat is narrow rather than strong. CAP 8.5 years.
name: Applied Industrial Technologies, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality technical industrial distributor, moat 5/10 with ROIC around 20% — but at $330.48 the OE yield is only 3.53% and the weighted IRR is 6.92%; it clears 15% only near $113.03.
